title: The Pension on Monte Trinità: the Pythagorean League, the Two Mountains, and the Man Who Pointed at the Hill
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Berlin, four men found a league
stops.date_confidence: The year 1884 is attested by the gusto-graeser.de essay 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund' and by de.wikipedia's article on Robert Springer. No month or day is given in any source, so both default to 01.
stops.campa: Four men put their names to a league in Berlin: Robert Springer the writer, Johannes Guttzeit the officer turned nature-preacher, Otto Rabe the agricultural economist, and Max Engelmann, of whom no source records a birth year, a birthplace, or a trade. They call it the Bund der Pythagoräer. The doctrine is two and a half thousand years old and the application is domestic: what a German eats, what he wears, what his house is made of. Engelmann is a founder, not a follower. It is the first time his name enters any record that survives.
suggested_refs: The founding of the Bund der Pythagoräer, Berlin 1884, in Hermann Müller's essay on the Bruder-Bund
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Berlin, the motto set down
stops.date_confidence: Undated within 1884; the motto is given by the gusto-graeser.de essay as the League's founding statement. Month and day default to 01, as for the founding stop.
stops.campa: The League writes its rule in two lines and prints it in the reformed spelling its members insist on, doubled consonants struck out as waste. Pythagoras supplies the prohibition, Plato supplies the aim: moderation and strength, wisdom and love. No German source translates it and none needs to. A vegetarian society in the Bismarck decade is not proposing a diet. It is proposing that the last four centuries took a wrong turning and that the correction is available at the table, tonight, without permission from anyone.
stops.quote: Unser Grundsaz: Ni Fleisch, ni Fisch! (Pythagoras). Unser Zil: Mässigkeit und Stärke, Weisheit und Libe! (Plato).
stops.quote_source: Founding motto of the Bund der Pythagoräer, 1884, quoted in Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF. Reform-orthography spelling is original to the source.
suggested_refs: The 1884 motto of the Bund der Pythagoräer in its original reform orthography
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Hanover, Enkarpa comes off the press
stops.date_confidence: Hannover 1884 is the imprint given in de.wikipedia's bibliography for Robert Springer and repeated in the gusto-graeser.de essay. Month and day unrecorded, both defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: Springer publishes the League's foundational book at Hanover: Enkarpa, a cultural history of mankind in the light of Pythagorean teaching. He derives vegetarianism from the doctrine of soul-purification and cites Porphyry on the gentleness owed to animals. It is the only theoretical apparatus the League will ever have. Engelmann's name is not on the title page; it is on the founding list. Springer is sixty-seven, born in Berlin in the year after Waterloo, and he has one year left to live.
suggested_refs: Robert Springer, Enkarpa. Culturgeschichte der Menschheit im Lichte der pythagoräischen Lehre, Hannover 1884
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Berlin, the league under its other name
stops.date_confidence: de.wikipedia's Springer article dates this founding only to 1884. Midyear is a placeholder chosen to separate the stop from the Pythagoräer-Bund founding and carries no evidential weight. Whether the two bodies are one is not stated by any source found.
stops.campa: German Wikipedia records the same four men founding a body of a different name in the same year: the Internationaler Bund für konsequente Humanität, the International League for Consistent Humanity. Springer, Guttzeit, Rabe, Engelmann. The founder lists are identical, and no reachable source says whether this is the Pythagoräer-Bund under a second name, an umbrella above it, or a separate association altogether. The atlas records both and joins neither. Engelmann's first documented act exists twice, under two names.
suggested_refs: de.wikipedia's account of the Internationaler Bund für konsequente Humanität, 1884
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Berlin, Rabe's first pamphlet
stops.date_confidence: 1885 attested as the imprint year of the Erste Flugschrift des Bundes der Pythagoräer, Berlin, self-published. Month and day unrecorded, both defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: Otto Rabe issues the League's first pamphlet from Berlin at his own expense, on the high cultural significance of a flesh-and-bloodless diet, offered as a contribution toward solving the social question. The argument is not about meat. The Pythagorean view of life, he writes, presses for a thoroughgoing reform of dwelling, of clothing, of every habit, of the whole manner of a man's living, in order to reduce his needs and by that means increase his independence. Monte Verità will be built on that sentence sixteen years later.
stops.quote: dringt nicht nur auf di Rückker zur Pflanzenkost; ir Streben richtet sich auf eine durchgreifende Reform in der Wonung, Kleidung, in allen Gewonheiten, kurz in der ganzen Lebensweise des Menschen. Si hat es sich zur Aufgabe gestellt, di Bedürfnisse des Menschen zu verringern und dadurch seine Unabhängigkeit zu erhöhen.
stops.quote_source: Otto Rabe, 'Di hohe Kulturbedeutung der fleisch- und blutlosen Ernarung des Menschen. Ein Beitrag zur Losung der sozialen Frage' (Erste Flugschrift des Bundes der Pythagoräer, Berlin, self-published, 1885), p.15, quoted in Hermann Müller, gusto-graeser.de PDF. The grammatical subject in the source is 'Die pythagorische Lebensanschauung', the Pythagorean view of life.
suggested_refs: Otto Rabe's Erste Flugschrift des Bundes der Pythagoräer, Berlin 1885
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Munich-Thalkirchen, Diefenbach writes to Engelmann
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by the gusto-graeser.de essay, citing the Diefenbach Nachlass at the Archiv der Deutschen Jugendbewegung, Burg Ludwigstein. The Nachlass itself was not consulted; the letter reaches this journey only through that essay.
stops.campa: The painter Karl Wilhelm Diefenbach, robed, barefoot, already gathering disciples on the edge of Munich, writes to Max Engelmann. Love is the formula for the redemption of mankind. True love overcomes everything, even disgust. To be a man means to love. And then, without transition, a whole myth already hovers around me. The letter survives in the Diefenbach papers at Burg Ludwigstein. It is the only document in the entire dossier addressed to Engelmann by name, and it reaches him fifteen years before either man sees Ticino.
stops.quote: Liebe ist die Formel zur Erlösung der Menschheit. Wahre Liebe überwindet alles, auch den Ekel. Mensch sein heisst lieben. Gott ist die Liebe, Gott ähnlich zu werden des Menschen Bestimmung. ... Ein ganzer Mythos umschwebt mich jetzt schon.
stops.quote_source: Karl Wilhelm Diefenbach, letter to Max Engelmann, 22 June 1885, Munich-Thalkirchen; Diefenbach Nachlass, Archiv der Deutschen Jugendbewegung, Burg Ludwigstein, quoted in Hermann Müller, gusto-graeser.de PDF
suggested_refs: The Diefenbach Nachlass, Archiv der Deutschen Jugendbewegung, Burg Ludwigstein
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Berlin, Springer dies
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by de.wikipedia, 'Robert Springer (Schriftsteller)': born 23 November 1816 in Berlin, died 21 October 1885 in Berlin.
stops.campa: Robert Springer dies in Berlin, sixty-eight years old, thirteen months after founding the League and one year after printing its book. The gusto-graeser.de essay states plainly that the group disintegrated in consequence: it had a theorist and no institution. Guttzeit takes what is left of it. Engelmann, whatever he was to the League, is now a member of a body whose author is dead and whose name is about to change to something with no Greek in it at all.
suggested_refs: Robert Springer's grave and Berlin dates, 23 November 1816 to 21 October 1885
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Berlin, the league renamed
stops.date_confidence: The renaming is undated in the source, which hedges it further with 'Es scheint, dass er nach dem Tod von Springer...'. Springer died 21 October 1885, so the change falls after that. 1886 is this journey's placeholder for an event the sources place only in the years following, and is not attested.
stops.campa: Guttzeit gives the Pythagoräer-Bund a new direction and a new name: Bund für volle Menschlichkeit, League for Full Humanity, subtitled brotherhood and re-naturalization. Its journal is called Bruder, and from the journal the group takes its other name, the Bruder-Bund. Pythagoras drops out of the letterhead. No source says whether Engelmann stayed through the change or left with the Greek. Here the record on him closes, and it does not open again for some fifteen years.
suggested_refs: Der Bruder: Zeitschrift des Bundes für volle Menschlichkeit, edited by Johannes Friedrich Guttzeit
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Monte Monescia, Ascona, a monastery that is never built
stops.date_confidence: Around 1889 per en.wikipedia and de.wikipedia, 'Monte Verità'; no month given, defaulted to 01. The coordinate is inherited byte-identical from the corpus pin for Monte Verità in laban.journey.json. de.wikipedia's geo-API gives the true summit as 46.15885, 8.76287, about 250 metres southwest; the corpus pin is kept so that the hill is one point on the atlas.
stops.campa: Alfredo Pioda, a Ticinese politician, plans a theosophical monastery on the vineyard hill above Ascona together with Franz Hartmann and Constance Wachtmeister of Blavatsky's circle. They mean to call it Fraternitas. Nothing is built. The hill stays what it is, a phylloxera-killed vineyard with shepherds' livestock on it, and the deed stays with Pioda for eleven more years. Every traveler the atlas will send up this slope, Hesse, Laban, Wigman, Perrottet, Jung, climbs ground first cleared in somebody's head as a cloister.
suggested_refs: Alfredo Pioda's unbuilt Fraternitas project on Monte Monescia, c. 1889

stops.name: Veldes, the light and water cure at Bled
stops.date_confidence: Rikli's Naturheilanstalt at Veldes is long established by this date. 1899 is the year de.wikipedia's 'Monte Verità' places the meeting of Ida Hofmann and Henri Oedenkoven there, with Karl Gräser taking a cure at the same time; month unrecorded, defaulted to 01. Engelmann's own presence at Bled is nowhere attested and is a corpus reconstruction.
stops.campa: At Veldes in the Slovene Alps, Arnold Rikli treats patients with sun, air and water and nothing else, unclothed in the light for as long as the light lasts. In 1899 Ida Hofmann and Henri Oedenkoven meet at his establishment while Karl Gräser is taking a cure there. The corpus holds that Engelmann's therapies came out of this house. No German source connects Rikli to Engelmann at all: the gusto-graeser.de essay never names Rikli, and calls Engelmann's place a vegetarian pension and nothing further.
suggested_refs: Arnold Rikli's Naturheilanstalt at Veldes (Bled), where Hofmann and Oedenkoven met in 1899

stops.name: Monti sopra Locarno, the German settles above the lake
stops.date_confidence: Undated. The gusto-graeser.de essay says only 'vor 1900'; de.wikipedia says he had settled at Monti sopra Locarno, presumably as a candidate for Pioda's unbuilt monastery, and gives no year. 1898 is this journey's placeholder inside the window the sources allow, and is not attested.
stops.campa: Engelmann comes south and stops above Locarno, on the terrace of chestnut and vine the maps call Monti and the people on it call Monte Trinità. German Wikipedia offers a reason inside its own quotation marks: presumably as a candidate for the monastery Pioda never built. He is forty-something, or sixty-something, since no source gives a birth year. He opens a vegetarian pension. Five kilometres west across the Maggia delta, on the hill he did not get to live on, the shepherds are still grazing Pioda's dead vineyard.
suggested_refs: Monti sopra Locarno, the terrace above the town, called Monte Trinità locally
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Monte Trinità, the vegetarian house
stops.date_confidence: The pension is attested in existence for 1900 by Ida Hofmann's memoir, and 'vor 1900' by the gusto-graeser.de essay. Month unrecorded, defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: The house keeps no meat and no fish, per the rule of 1884. Ida Hofmann's memoir calls it the pension of the Engelmann couple; the same gusto-graeser.de essay speaks elsewhere of Engelmann's Anhänger, long-haired followers. Marriage or small community, the two sources do not agree and are not reconciled here. What is certain is a German-run vegetarian boarding house above Locarno in the last years of the century, standing in the road of everyone walking south for the same set of reasons.
suggested_refs: The Engelmann vegetarian pension on Monte Trinità above Locarno
sources: Ida Hofmann, Monte Verità, p.15, quoted in Hermann Müller, gusto-graeser.de PDF
Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Locarno, the town at the foot of the terrace
stops.date_confidence: A placeholder date for a continuous residence the sources do not date. Locarno is the town below Engelmann's terrace throughout his documented Ticino years, and the place of publication given for his 1918 tract.
stops.campa: Below the vineyard steps lies Locarno on Lago Maggiore: customs post, lake steamer pier, the last Italian-speaking town before the Alps close. Germans arrive here all through the 1890s carrying the same short list of demands, sun, vegetables, no clothes, no landlord. They ask in the town for somebody who lives that way and the town sends them up the hill. Eleven years later Rudolf Steiner will lecture in these streets on esoteric Christianity, and the colony across the water will send its founders down to listen.
suggested_refs: Locarno on Lago Maggiore, port of entry for the German life reform in Ticino

stops.name: Monte Brè, Lugano, the sanitarium the corpus places here
stops.date_confidence: This is the corpus's siting, not the German sources'. Essay 191_goethe_italian_exit.md and one clause of en.wikipedia's 'Monte Verità' put Engelmann's establishment on Monte Brè above Lugano; de.wikipedia, Ida Hofmann's memoir and the gusto-graeser.de essay all put it above Locarno, fifty-five kilometres north on a different lake. The contradiction is recorded, not resolved. Coordinate is de.wikipedia's summit of Monte Brè, 46.008558 and 8.986473, rounded.
stops.campa: The corpus puts him here instead: a sanitarium on Monte Brè above Lugano, offering Rikli's helio-hydroscopic cures in the nude, sun and water on unclothed bodies at the foot of the mountain Goethe rounded in 1788 on the vanished stretch of his Italian journey. No German record of any Engelmann institution on this mountain has been found in four languages of search. English Wikipedia carries a single clause supporting it and is most likely mistranslating the German. The atlas pins both mountains and lets the argument stand.
suggested_refs: Monte Brè above Lugano, the corpus's siting of Engelmann's sanitarium

stops.name: Lago di Lugano, the lacuna in Goethe's road
stops.date_confidence: The lake is the corpus's own frame for Engelmann, taken from QUEUE.md line 75, which files him as life-reformer of the Pythagorean League at Lago di Lugano. The coordinate is the interlock pin for the lake. Neither the queue entry nor the essay is externally corroborated, and the date is a placeholder.
stops.campa: The atlas queue files Engelmann under this lake, not the other one. The reason is Goethe. In May 1788 he came northwest out of Como, crossed into the Italian-speaking bailiwicks of the old Confederacy, passed Riva San Vitale and Lugano and Campione, and left almost nothing written about any of it. The corpus calls that silence the lacuna of Lago di Lugano and puts Engelmann's naked patients inside it a century later. It is a placement made by an essay, and the essay says so on its own page.
suggested_refs: QUEUE.md line 75, Engelmann filed at Lago di Lugano; Goethe's undocumented passage of May 1788

segments.name: Autumn 1900, the Brothers at the Door

stops.name: Munich, the letters end in a meeting
stops.date_confidence: October 1900 attested by de.wikipedia, 'Monte Verità'; no day given, defaulted to 01. The coordinate is Marienplatz, a placeholder, since no venue is named. The corpus adds the Gräser brothers to this meeting and makes Engelmann the source of its Ascona information; neither is externally attested.
stops.campa: An intensive correspondence between Henri Oedenkoven, son of an Antwerp industrialist, and Ida Hofmann, a pianist from Montenegro, leads in October to a meeting in Munich. German Wikipedia has the two of them at it and nobody else. The corpus seats the Gräser brothers at the same table and has Engelmann telling them, by letter or in person it does not say, about a failed theosophist colony in Ticino. The direction that information travels is the one thing the two accounts flatly reverse.
suggested_refs: The October 1900 Munich meeting of Oedenkoven and Hofmann

stops.name: Ascona, the brothers on their scouting march
stops.date_confidence: The gusto-graeser.de essay places the Gräser brothers' Erkundungszug in 'Spätherbst 1900'; de.wikipedia and en.wikipedia date Engelmann's meeting with them to November 1900. Day unrecorded, defaulted to 01. The coordinate is Ascona town, the district they are searching, not a named site.
stops.campa: Karl Gräser, an officer who has resigned his commission, and his brother Gustav, a poet who will refuse salt, money and capital letters, walk the shore of Lago Maggiore looking for ground to buy. The German sources are exact about the sequence. The brothers are already in Ticino and already searching when they come upon the pension and its keeper; they stumble on him, and he does not summon them. The corpus tells it the other way round, with Engelmann writing to Munich. Both versions stand in the atlas.
stops.quote: Auf diese Pension und ihren Inhaber stießen die Brüder Gräser auf ihrem Erkundungszug.
stops.quote_source: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF
suggested_refs: The Gräser brothers' Erkundungszug through Ticino, late autumn 1900
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Monte Trinità, arrival at dusk
stops.date_confidence: November 1900 is attested by de.wikipedia and en.wikipedia for Engelmann's meeting with the Gräser brothers. Ida Hofmann's memoir gives the hour, gegen die Abendstunde, but no date. The fifteenth is a placeholder inside the attested month.
stops.campa: Karl has written ahead to the others: here one finds people, long-haired ones, vegetarian pensions, come to us. After much searching and asking they fall in toward the evening hour on the pension of the Engelmann couple above Locarno. Ida Hofmann sets the scene down six years later in her memoir, and the sentence that follows it is the only line in the whole dossier describing Engelmann's conduct rather than his opinions. We were received most kindly.
stops.quote: "Hier findet man Menschen", "auch langhaarige - vegetarische Pensionen u.s.w." schrieb Karl, "kommet zu uns" und nach vielem Suchen und Fragen fielen wir dann gegen die Abendstunde in die Pension des Ehepaares Engelmann auf dem Monte Trinita oberhalb Locarno. Wir wurden freundlichst empfangen.
stops.quote_source: Ida Hofmann, Monte Verità, p.15, quoted in Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF
suggested_refs: Ida Hofmann, Monte Verità: Wahrheit ohne Dichtung (1906), p.15
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Monte Trinità, the hill pointed out
stops.date_confidence: Conjectural in the source itself, which writes 'Er wird sie auf das von den Locarneser Theosophen angekaufte Grundstück auf dem Hügel Monescia hingewiesen haben'. de.wikipedia and en.wikipedia say only that Engelmann met the brothers in November 1900 and probably drew their attention to Pioda's property. The day is a placeholder.
stops.campa: Somewhere in the conversation Engelmann tells his guests about the hill across the delta: a property the Locarno theosophists bought for a monastery and never used, standing empty above Ascona. The German is a future perfect. He will have pointed them to it. The whole of his place in this atlas rests on that tense, and the source that names him as the hinge declines to swear to it. He is a man known to history for one sentence he probably said at his own dinner table.
stops.quote: Er wird sie auf das von den Locarneser Theosophen angekaufte Grundstück auf dem Hügel Monescia hingewiesen haben.
stops.quote_source: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF
suggested_refs: The Locarno theosophists' Monescia parcel, bought by Pioda and never used
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Monte Monescia, Ascona, the vineyard bought
stops.date_confidence: de.wikipedia dates the purchase to autumn 1900: Oedenkoven, Hofmann, Karl Gräser, Gusto Gräser and Lotte Hattemer find the ground after some weeks of searching in Ascona and buy it from Alfredo Pioda. Month unrecorded; December is set as the late edge of that autumn. The corpus essay dates the acquisition to 1902, which is in fact the year of the naming. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from laban.journey.json.
stops.campa: After some weeks of searching, Henri Oedenkoven, Ida Hofmann, Karl and Gusto Gräser and Lotte Hattemer buy the hill from Pioda: four hectares of dead vineyard with shepherds' livestock on it. The corpus records four acres and so understates the ground by more than half. They begin putting up huts. Engelmann does not go with them. He stays on his own terrace above Locarno and keeps the boarding house, and the record of his life goes quiet again for five years.
suggested_refs: The 1900 purchase of the Monescia parcel from Alfredo Pioda, four hectares

stops.name: Monte Verità, the naming
stops.date_confidence: 1902 attested by de.wikipedia for the naming only: 'gaben dieser 1902 den Namen Monte Verità'. Month and day unrecorded, both defaulted to 01. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from laban.journey.json.
stops.campa: Two years after the purchase the founders give the hill a name: Monte Verità, the Mountain of Truth. It has the rule of 1884 inside it, no flesh and no fish, and it has Rabe's sentence inside it, reduce the need and enlarge the freedom by that much. None of the founders ever joined the Bund der Pythagoräer and none of them would have been able to recite its motto. The doctrine travelled from Berlin to this hill by way of a boarding house and a wrong turning.
suggested_refs: The naming of Monte Verità, 1902

stops.name: Ticino, the pages on Goethe
stops.date_confidence: Entirely undated. The gusto-graeser.de essay says only that Engelmann 'hatte über Goethe geschrieben', a pluperfect placing the writing before the 1905 tract; no title, publisher, place or year is given anywhere. 1903 is a placeholder carrying no evidential weight, and the coordinate is his known residence, not an imprint.
stops.campa: He writes about Goethe. That is the whole of what the record says: one pluperfect clause in a secondary essay, with no title, no publisher, no year, and no copy found in any catalogue searched. The corpus's own doorway to Engelmann was Goethe's lost week on Lago di Lugano, and the one thing Engelmann is known to have written before 1905 is about Goethe. The text is missing. The coincidence is entered here as a coincidence and nothing is built on it.
suggested_refs: Engelmann's untraced writing on Goethe, undated, title unknown
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Ticino, Das Germanentum und sein Verfall
stops.date_confidence: 1905 attested by the gusto-graeser.de essay for this title only. No month, no place of publication, no publisher is given. The coordinate is Engelmann's known residence at the time and is a placeholder, not an imprint.
stops.campa: Engelmann publishes on Teutonism and its decline. No copy has been located and the essay that names it says nothing beyond the title and the year. The vegetarian who founded a league on Pythagoras and Plato in 1884 is writing about Germanic decay in 1905, from a hillside in Italian-speaking Switzerland, twenty years after receiving a letter telling him that love is the formula for the redemption of mankind. The book that would explain the distance between those positions is the book that is gone.
suggested_refs: Karl Max Engelmann, Das Germanentum und sein Verfall (1905), untraced
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Monte Trinità, Der Uranische Staat is written
stops.date_confidence: The gusto-graeser.de essay's body text dates the tract 1917; the same document's bibliography gives the published imprint as Monte Trinità, Locarno, 1918. Both years stand uncorrected in one source and are not reconciled here. This stop takes the body text's year and the next stop takes the imprint's.
stops.campa: In the fourth year of the war Engelmann writes a constitution. Der Uranische Staat als Pflichterfüllung des Stärkeren: the Uranian State as the duty-fulfilment of the stronger. It sketches a future life-reform polity on frankly elitist terms, the strong governing as an obligation laid on them rather than a right they hold. Its author has been keeping a vegetarian boarding house above Locarno for nearly twenty years while Europe filled the ground north of the Alps with trenches.
suggested_refs: Karl Max Engelmann, Der Uranische Staat als Pflichterfüllung des Stärkeren
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Monte Trinità, the imprint and the closing verse
stops.date_confidence: 1918 is the imprint year in the gusto-graeser.de essay's own bibliography, which gives the place of publication as Monte Trinità, Locarno. Month and day unrecorded, both defaulted to 01. No digitized copy of the pamphlet was located; the verse is known only as an excerpt from p.74 quoted in that essay.
stops.campa: The tract is printed with the mountain itself as its place of publication: Monte Trinità, Locarno, 1918. It closes on four lines of verse. Ruin lives in the narrow of dull walls; get out of the pressing crush of the cities; may a receptive feeling bloom in you for the eternal primal songs of a freer allness. It is the oldest argument the life reform ever made, set in rhyme by a man who made it in Berlin in 1884 and was still making it thirty-four years later on the same terms.
stops.quote: Verderben wohnt in dumpfer Mauern Enge! Fort aus der Städte drückendem Gewühl! Für freier Allheit ew'ge Urgesänge erblüh Euch ein empfängliches Gefühl!
stops.quote_source: Karl Max Engelmann, 'Der Uranische Staat als Pflichterfüllung des Stärkeren' (Monte Trinità, Locarno, 1918), p.74, quoted in Hermann Müller, gusto-graeser.de PDF
suggested_refs: Der Uranische Staat als Pflichterfüllung des Stärkeren, Monte Trinità, Locarno, 1918, p.74
sources: Hermann Müller, 'Bruder-Bund und Pythagoräer-Bund', gusto-graeser.de PDF

stops.name: Monte Trinità, the uranian word
stops.date_confidence: Speculation, and the source says so: 'kann angenommen werden, dass...'. No direct biographical statement about Engelmann's own orientation exists in any source found. The date sits inside the tract's imprint year purely to place the stop, and asserts nothing.
stops.campa: Uranisch is not a neutral adjective in 1918. It is the word men used of themselves under Paragraph 175, taken from Ulrichs, taken in turn from Plato's heavenly Aphrodite. The gusto-graeser.de essay proposes that persecuted homosexuality among some members, Guttzeit included, may have supplied a motive for founding the League in the first place, and reads Engelmann's title back into 1884 as its evidence. The essay says only that this can be assumed. No document says anything about Engelmann.
suggested_refs: The nineteenth-century vocabulary of Uranism, from Karl Heinrich Ulrichs to Paragraph 175
